institutionName: UiT The Arctic University of Norway

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The possibility of taking courses in indigenous studies, which is a program/field that is not possible to study in UCPH

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UiT provided all the necessary information and it was easy to get help/further information if needed

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were 3 welcome days where we got a lot of information about life in Tromsø, academic life at UiT, formal registrations in terms of taxes, residence permits etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very easy - Samskipnaden - The UiT housing office were very helpful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very easy to get around in Tromsø with public busses, cross country skis etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Good facilities, fair prices and good service from Samskipnaden

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit difficult but durable

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy to register for the different courses but a bit harder to get pre-approvals before going to Tromsø - the whole process is very bureaucratic and everything has to be approved both by UiT and UCPH which makes it a very time-consuming process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: UiT administrative staff were very helpfull

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted and applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to participate in the introweek - there you can get help with the whole process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally satisfied with the courses I participated in

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was similar to the level in UCPH - not too hard, not too easy

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar - same Scandinavian teaching environment

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Visual Ethnography (10 ECTS)
2) Indigenous Culture, Resource Management and Human Rights (10 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Indigenous Culture, Resource Management and Human Rights - a very good anthropology course within the field of indigenous studies

questions.answer: Food and basic grosseries are obviously very expensive in Norway but that was expected

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A lot of opportunities in the natural landscapes, good skiing facilities, good gym, good nightlife etc. - generally a lot of opportunities

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Several sports clubs, film clubs, skiing classes etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Cross country skiing is a must

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking/skiing in Kvaløya, trip to Senja and Lofoten, dog sledding etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - very similar to Danish culture

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak Danish to the Norwegian students - its a great advantage that we understand each other and have a lot in common

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Norwegian people are generally very welcoming and friendly

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Bring warm clothes, a good camera for the northers lights and buy spikes immediately when you arrive (its extremely slippery during the winter so spikes are a must)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to live in the Arctic surrounded by amazing natural landscapes

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
